Subject: Re: Private endpoints — outbound IPs / firewall acceptance window

Jack / team — here's the technical summary you can hand to ops. I've kept it short and prescriptive so it can be pasted into change tickets.

1) Recommended deployment model (summary)
- Preferred: restrict egress to a small set of static IPs via a customer-managed NAT gateway or egress proxy. This gives predictable addressing for firewall policy and simplifies auditing.
- Alternate: if NAT is not possible, allow listed CIDRs on the private endpoint hosts directly (less recommended due to host churn).

2) Required outbound destinations (canonical list)
- Control plane API (TLS): 52.41.210.12/32, 52.41.210.13/32
- Metrics & telemetry (TLS → s3-compatible ingest): 52.41.211.0/24
- Model artifact fetch / staging (TLS): 34.99.120.0/24
- Healthchecks / failover probes (TLS): 34.99.121.45/32
Note: we publish these as a CSV (redwood-egress-ip-list.csv) and version them when we add ranges. Use the CSV import rather than ad-hoc typing.

3) Ports & protocols
- TCP 443 (HTTPS / TLS) — mandatory for control plane, metrics, artifact fetch
- TCP 80 — optional (redirects) but not required if your NAT does HTTP→HTTPS redirect
- UDP 123 — NTP recommended outbound to your managed time service (if you do not already have time sync internally)
- DNS (UDP/TCP 53) — required for name resolution if you do not force-mapping in your proxy; we recommend egress only to your internal DNS forwarder or to a restricted set of resolvers.

4) TLS & identity
- All Redwood control-plane endpoints require TLS; we support mTLS for higher assurance. If you enable mTLS, you can further restrict destinations to the control-plane endpoint CIDRs above.

5) Failure and fallback behavior
- If control-plane endpoints are unreachable, the private deployment will continue serving cached model weights and accept inference requests for in-flight sessions; new model pulls and control-plane-driven rollout changes will fail until connectivity is restored.
- We recommend configuring your NAT/proxy with a retry policy and a secondary egress path (different public IP) for the control plane to avoid single-host egress failures during scheduled patching.

6) Test checklist for 2026-09-02 window
- From a private endpoint host: curl -I https://52.41.210.12/health (expect 200)
- Push a small telemetry payload to metrics endpoint (TLS) and confirm ingestion in Redwood Console
- Pull a test artifact from 34.99.120.7:443

7) Security recommendations (ops-friendly)
- Block outbound to all CIDRs except the CSV list and your internal services.
- Log TLS SNI for outbound connections and retain logs for 30 days for the pilot.
- If you require SOC2 evidence, request our SOC2 excerpt (we've attached relevant pages).

Attachments (in this message): private-endpoint-firewall-extract.txt (text with the short rule-set)

If you want, Priyom and I can jump on a 30-minute troubleshooting call during your change window to watch the healthchecks.

—Rishi

Redwood Inference
